clips.text: What if you could hold your breath for an hour? Not with gills. With the body you already have.
One man fell asleep at the bottom of a pool and didn't breathe for 29 minutes. His body just... waited.
The urge to breathe isn't oxygen running out. It's carbon dioxide building up. Your alarm lies to you.
Cold water on your face slows your heart. Your spleen squeezes out extra oxygen. You were born with dive gear.
So here's the test: if you could hold your breath for an hour, what's the first thing you'd do underwater?
You can barely last 30 seconds underwater — but one man fell asleep at the bottom of a pool and didn't breathe for 29 minutes.
